failure.description: Canonical acceptance first failed because the workflow read canonical_schema from the top level of a JSON Schema document. After that repair, acceptance correctly exposed that the existing proof record used a legacy object shape and lacked canonical required fields.
failure.root_cause: Validation logic and proof record had drifted from the canonical NAYA_ACTION_V1 schema model.
failure.repair: Corrected compatibility-schema inspection to use properties.canonical_schema.const and rebuilt this proof record to the canonical field structure with fail-closed unknown runtime state.
failure.safeguard: Future acceptance must validate the proof record against the canonical schema shape rather than treating required-field presence alone as full schema conformance.

lesson: A JSON Schema document describes instance properties; its declared fields belong under properties unless the schema itself intentionally defines a custom keyword.
Required-field presence is not equivalent to schema validity when nested objects use additionalProperties=false.
The canonical proof record must evolve with the canonical machine schema, and proof scope must remain HEAD^ of the record commit.
Failure is repair information; stop at the first real defect and continue the complete acceptance chain after repair.
